web_accessibility.summary: BrowserStack Web Accessibility: WCAG accessibility results for websites and web apps. List the account's Workflow Analyzer reports, Website Scanner scans and their runs, Automated Tests projects and builds, and Assisted Test reports, each with the id the accessibility issue tool reads. Read what the dashboard shows: custom dashboards and their scores, a build or scan run's report (overview, test cases, issues by rule or WCAG guideline, affected components, page logs), comparisons of two runs, scan trends and settings, and the signed-in user. Writes, each needing approval: re-run a scan, hide or un-hide issues, settle needs-review issues, submit or undo a bulk review, link issues to a ticket. Dashboard capabilities use an agent-scoped token; the user's own role and plan still apply. It also keeps the false-positive memory: issues users marked not real. Mobile apps are a separate product.

capabilities.name: list_workflow_analyzer_reports

query.name: limit
query.description: Reports per page, 10 to 99. Send the same limit with every next_page: the token carries only the page number, so a different limit shifts the pages. 100 is not offered because it returns 30 reports and says there is no next page.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.nextPage token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Workflow Analyzer reports newest first, with each report's id, name, creator, status, settings and issue counts - use this to find someone's latest reports, a report by name, or the id that reads its issues.
guidance: Link a report as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/workflow-analyzer/report?ids={id}, with the bare id (39252, never workflowScan:39252); several reports open together as ids=1,2,3. The same address works in every region.
id is the workflowReportId fetchAccessibilityIssues takes to read a report's issues.

There is no filter by person, name or date: the list holds every report in the account, newest first. For someone's latest reports, read pages in order, with limit 99 to need fewer, and keep the rows whose createdBy.name or createdBy.id is theirs, stopping once you have enough.
Paging is data.pagination.hasNext and data.pagination.nextPage; send nextPage back as next_page with the same limit.
The settings sit under scanSettings, with wcagVersion an object of label and value, and the counts under issueSummary; the public API docs show both flat.
A limit outside 10 to 100 is not refused: a page of 20 comes back, and error says why.
These are web reports from the browser extension. A mobile app's Workflow Analyzer reports are App Accessibility manual reports, listed there.

capabilities.name: list_website_scanner_scans

query.name: limit
query.description: Scans per page, 10 to 25. Above 25 the page still holds 25 scans but the next page starts past the ones in between, so they are skipped. With next_page, omit limit or send the same value: a different one answers 422.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.nextPage token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'. page_size is not read either.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Website Scanner scans, most recently run first, with each scan's id, name, creator, dashboard link and latest run - use this to find a scan by name or person, or the scan and run ids that read its issues.
guidance: id is the scanId fetchAccessibilityIssues takes, and lastScanDetails.scanRunId is the scanRunId of the scan's latest run; list_website_scanner_scan_runs gives the earlier ones.
scanUrl is the scan's report on the Accessibility dashboard: the link to give a user.

There is no filter: current_user_id, team, page and page_size are not read, and every scan in the account comes back. For one person's scans keep the rows whose createdBy.name or createdBy.id is theirs.
Pages run from the most recently scanned, but the rows within a page are sorted by scan id, so order them by lastScanDetails.lastScanDate.
createdBy is an object of id and name, not the bare user id the public docs show.
lastScanDetails.error can hold a message while scanStatus is completed: some pages failed, and reportSummary.failure counts them.

capabilities.name: list_website_scanner_scan_runs

path_params.name: scan_id
path_params.description: The scan's id, from list_website_scanner_scans or the answer of startAccessibilityScan. A scan's name is not accepted.

query.name: limit
query.description: Runs per page, 10 to 100. With next_page, omit limit or send the same value: a different one answers 422.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.nextPage token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'.

capabilities.intent: List one Website Scanner scan's runs newest first, with each run's id, date, issue and component counts and how many pages loaded - use this to pick an earlier run or follow a site's issues over time.
guidance: Link a run as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/site-scanner/projects/{scan name}/builds?thBuildId={thBuildId}, with the scan's display name (name in list_website_scanner_scans, URL-encoded), never the CS_<name>_CS projectName. The same address works in every region.
id is the scanRunId fetchAccessibilityIssues takes with this scan's scanId, also as compareWith.
Runs are ordered by scanDate, newest first. A run started by hand can carry a later id than a newer scheduled run, so do not order them by id.
reportSummary.failure counts the pages that did not load in that run; their issues are missing from its count.
An unknown scan answers 404 'Scan builds not found'.

issues, componentCount and reportSummary are null on runs whose summary this list does not hold (often every run but the latest): null means not recorded here, not zero. get_website_scanner_scan_trends gives the issue count of every completed run.

capabilities.name: list_automated_tests_projects

query.name: limit
query.description: Projects per page, 10 to 100 (default 10). With next_page, omit limit or send the same value: a different one answers 400.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.next_page token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Automated Tests projects newest first, with each project's id, name and creation date - use this to find the project name that narrows its builds.
guidance: There is no name filter: name and search are not read, and the whole list comes back, newest first.
list_automated_tests_builds narrows to a project by its name (project_name), not by this id.
Paging here is snake_case: data.pagination.has_next and data.pagination.next_page.
Website Scanner scans are not projects here; list them with list_website_scanner_scans.

capabilities.name: list_automated_tests_builds

query.name: project_name
query.description: Keeps one project's builds: its full name, in any letter case. Part of a name matches nothing. Only this snake_case name is read: projectId, project_id and projectName are ignored, and every project's builds come back.

query.name: limit
query.description: Builds per page, 10 to 100 (default 10). With next_page, omit limit or send the same value: a different one answers 400.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.next_page token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'. Send project_name again, unchanged: a different one answers 400.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Automated Tests builds newest first, or one project's, with each build's id, number, name, creator, status and issue counts - use this to find a suite's latest run, someone's builds, or the build id that reads its issues.
guidance: Link a build as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/automated-tests/projects/{project name}/builds/{name}/{buildNumber}?thBuildId={id}, every value from the same row and URL-encoded (a space is %20). The row has only projectId: take the project name from list_automated_tests_projects, or use list_build_report_runs, whose rows carry projectName. Without thBuildId the page loads nothing. The same address works in every region.
id is the 40-character build id fetchAccessibilityIssues takes as buildId, the thBuildId in the build's dashboard link.
A project_name that matches no project answers 200 with data null and info ['No Projects found']: no match, not an error.
Builds that ran without accessibility checks are left out, so a page can hold fewer rows than limit.
There is no filter by person: keep the rows whose createdBy.name or createdBy.userId is theirs.
summary (page, component and issue counts, test health) is present only on a completed build that ran tests; a completed build with no tests reads status failed.
Paging here is snake_case: data.pagination.has_next and data.pagination.next_page.

capabilities.name: list_assisted_test_reports

query.name: limit
query.description: Reports per page, 10 to 99. Send the same limit with every next_page: the token carries only the page number, so a different limit shifts the pages. 100 is not offered because it returns 30 reports and says there is no next page.

query.name: next_page
query.description: The data.pagination.nextPage token from the previous page, sent back as given. page is not read: a call sending it gets the first page every time. A changed or expired token answers 422 'Invalid pagination token'.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Assisted Test reports newest first, with each report's id, name, creator, status, test type and issue counts - use this to find a guided keyboard, forms or other assisted check someone ran.
guidance: Link a report as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/assisted-test/report?ar_ids={id}, with the bare id (never assistiveTest:<id>). The same address works in every region.
fetchAccessibilityIssues does not read Assisted Test reports: the counts here are what an agent can get, and the report itself is read on the Accessibility dashboard.
scanSettings.assistedTestType is a number: 0 keyboard, 1 interactive elements, 2 modals, 3 forms, 4 images, 5 layout, 6 tables, 7 responsiveness.

There is no filter by person, name or date: the list holds every report in the account, newest first; read pages in order, with limit 99 to need fewer, and keep the rows whose createdBy.name or createdBy.id is theirs.
Paging is data.pagination.hasNext and data.pagination.nextPage; send nextPage back as next_page with the same limit.

capabilities.name: list_custom_dashboards

query.name: query
query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the dashboard name OR the creator's full name. Omit it to list every dashboard.

capabilities.intent: List the account's custom dashboards newest first, with each one's id, name, creator and cached issue count, page count and score - use this to find a dashboard by name or person, or the id the other custom dashboard capabilities take.
guidance: Link a dashboard as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/dashboards/{id}. The same address works in every region.
id is the {id} every get_custom_dashboard_* capability takes.
The list is not paginated: every dashboard comes back in one response, newest created first.

summary is a cache written the last time someone opened the dashboard, so it can be stale; summary.score is null when it was never computed or the dashboard has no scans. For current numbers call get_custom_dashboard_issue_summary and get_custom_dashboard_score_summary.
query matches the creator's name as well as the dashboard name, so a person's name finds their dashboards.
A 403 with code PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED means the account's plan has no Custom Dashboards; a team-scoped (UDAC team view) user sees only dashboards for their own team.

200.description: Every custom dashboard in the account, newest first, unpaginated.

summary.description: Cached figures from the last time the dashboard was opened.

score.description: Cached; null when never computed or no scans.

capabilities.name: get_custom_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Read one custom dashboard's settings and state: name, WCAG version, time frame, creator, when its scans were last refreshed, whether it has any scans, and its public link - use this before reading its summaries.
guidance: Check hasTests first: when it is false the dashboard has no scans, and get_custom_dashboard_issue_summary, get_custom_dashboard_category_summary and get_custom_dashboard_score_summary answer 500 with an empty body rather than zeros.
settings.wcagVersion is a display label such as 'WCAG 2.2 AA', not a code; settings.timeFrame is the look-back window in days.
hasBuildsDropped true means at least one scan pinned to the dashboard is no longer found (deleted or aged out); the dashboard shows the rest.
updatedAt is when the dashboard's scans were last fetched, not when its settings were edited.
publicLink.isEnabled false means no public link exists; when true, publicLink.link is the shareable URL.
groupingMode is 'new', 'old', 'mixed' or null (no scans): whether duplicate issues across pages are grouped.

200.description: One dashboard's settings and state, under metaData (not data).

updatedAt.description: When the scans were last fetched.

link.description: Present only when isEnabled is true.

hasTests.description: false = no scans; the summary capabilities then answer 500.

groupingMode.description: new, old, mixed, or null when there are no scans.

capabilities.name: list_custom_dashboard_scans
capabilities.intent: List the scans (builds) a custom dashboard is built from - each one's product, project, name, creator, last run time and a link to its own report - use this to see what feeds a dashboard or to open the underlying reports.
guidance: testType is the product: automated-tests, website-scanner, workflow-analyzer, assisted-test or lcnc. metadata counts the scans per testType.
reportLink is the scan's own report on the Accessibility dashboard: the link to give a user.
projectId and buildUuid identify the Automated Tests / Website Scanner build behind the row; groupingIdentifier is null for most scans.
Each row is the latest run of the pinned scan, so updatedAt is that run's time. An empty dashboard answers 200 with builds [] and metadata {}.
Not paginated: all scans come back at once.

200.description: The scans feeding the dashboard, with per-product counts.

testType.description: automated-tests, website-scanner, workflow-analyzer, assisted-test or lcnc.

metadata.description: Scan count per testType; only the types present appear; {} when empty.

capabilities.name: get_custom_dashboard_issue_summary
capabilities.intent: Count a custom dashboard's issues by severity (critical, serious, moderate, minor) across all its scans, with the total - use this for 'how many issues' or 'how many critical issues' on a dashboard.
guidance: These totals already merge and de-duplicate across the dashboard's scans: report them as they stand, and never add up the underlying reports instead, which double-counts.
issueCount is the sum of the four severities. duplicateIssueCount is how many issues were folded away as duplicates of another; it is already excluded from issueCount.
A dashboard with no scans (get_custom_dashboard hasTests false) answers 500 with an empty body, not zeros: check hasTests first.
Calling this also refreshes the cached summary.issueCount that list_custom_dashboards shows.

200.description: Issue counts by severity across the dashboard.

duplicateIssueCount.description: Duplicates folded away; not in issueCount.

capabilities.name: get_custom_dashboard_category_summary
capabilities.intent: Count a custom dashboard's issues by category (colour, ARIA, forms, keyboard and so on), largest first - use this for 'what kind of issues does this dashboard have most of'.
guidance: These totals already merge and de-duplicate across the dashboard's scans: report them as they stand, and never add up the underlying reports instead, which double-counts.
Every category is listed, including those at 0, sorted by count descending. category is the axe tag (e.g. cat.color); name is its display label.
On an RGAA dashboard the buckets are the 13 RGAA themes (category rgaa_theme_1 to rgaa_theme_13) instead of axe categories.
Counts include needs-review issues as well as confirmed ones, so they can exceed get_custom_dashboard_issue_summary on some dashboards.
The label for cat.name-role-value reads 'Alt-area'; that is the backend's label, not a different category.
A dashboard with no scans (get_custom_dashboard hasTests false) answers 500 with an empty body: check hasTests first.

200.description: Issue counts per category, every category listed, largest first.

category.description: axe tag such as cat.color, or rgaa_theme_N on RGAA dashboards.

capabilities.name: get_custom_dashboard_score_summary
capabilities.intent: Read a custom dashboard's accessibility score (0-100) and the per-severity pass/fail breakdown behind it - use this for 'what is this dashboard's score' or why it is low.
guidance: These totals already merge and de-duplicate across the dashboard's scans: report them as they stand, and never add up the underlying reports instead, which double-counts.
score is 0 to 100, higher is better.

Under impact, the bare severity key (critical, serious, moderate, minor) is the PERCENTAGE that failed at that severity, not an issue count; <severity>Passed and <severity>Failed are the counts of passed and failed checks feeding it. For issue counts use get_custom_dashboard_issue_summary.
A dashboard with no scans (get_custom_dashboard hasTests false) answers 500 with an empty body: check hasTests first.
Calling this also refreshes the cached summary.score that list_custom_dashboards shows.

200.description: Dashboard score 0-100 and per-severity pass/fail breakdown.

capabilities.name: list_accessibility_guidelines
capabilities.intent: Look up the full catalogue of accessibility guidelines - every WCAG success criterion and RGAA criterion and theme - with its number, name, description, level, principle and the regulations it belongs to - use this to explain what a guideline tag such as wcag143 means.
guidance: data is an object keyed by guideline tag (wcag111, wcag412, rgaa_1_1, rgaa_theme_1), not an array: look a tag up by key.
value is the human number (1.1.1 for wcag111, 1.1 for rgaa_1_1); level is A, AA or AAA for WCAG and null for RGAA; urls maps a WCAG version (2.0, 2.1, 2.2) or RGAA 4.1 to its reference page.
There is no filter: the whole catalogue of about 200 entries always comes back, so pick out the tags you need.
RGAA names are in French and their description is empty. assistive_tests is null for RGAA themes.
Each entry carries value, name, description, level, principle, regulations, urls and assistive_tests.

200.description: The whole guideline catalogue, as an object keyed by tag.

data.description: Keyed by guideline tag (wcag111, rgaa_1_1, rgaa_theme_1, ...); wcag111 shown as an example key.

level.description: A, AA or AAA; null for RGAA.
A, AA or AAA; null for RGAA.

capabilities.name: get_current_user_profile
capabilities.intent: Who am I: read the signed-in user's id, name, email, role, group (account) id, plan and plan features, RBAC permissions, and which accessibility products they have reports in - use this for 'my group id', 'what plan am I on', 'can I use X'.
guidance: Answer the user from plan_name, plan_features, permissions, rbac_role and product_status. Never mention internal flags to the user: in_ai_feature_fencing_exception_list, feature_flags, beta_access_requests, product_access_request, udac and eft_type are rollout and billing internals, not facts about their account.
The fields sit at the top level, with no success or data wrapper.
group_id is the account id; user_id is the numeric id that list_accessibility_reports takes as user_id and that createdBy.id shows in other lists.
Casing is mixed: most keys are snake_case, but customDashboardsStatus, trialGrant and remediationTrialGrant are camelCase.
For whether a feature is available read plan_features (feature codes) and customDashboardsStatus, not plan_type: a group can show plan_type 'free' while plan_name is a paid tier.
permissions lists the RBAC actions the user holds (e.g. dashboards_view, builds_delete); rbac_role is their role. A capability refused with 403 Forbidden usually traces to one missing here.
product_status says which products already have reports (has_workflow_analyzer_report and so on).

200.description: The signed-in user's profile, plan and permissions, at the top level with no wrapper.

plan_type.description: Can read free on a paid plan; use plan_features.

capabilities.name: list_accessibility_reports

query.name: product
query.description: Which manual product's reports to list. extension returns Workflow Analyzer and Assisted Test reports merged. Required: a missing product answers 422 'Parameter product is required'.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number, from 1. info.next is the next page or null on the last one.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Reports per page, 1 to 99.

query.name: query
query.description: Search on the report name.

query.name: user_id
query.description: Only reports created by this numeric user id (the user_id of get_current_user_profile, or createdBy.id of a row).

query.name: team_id
query.description: Only reports of this team (sub-group) id; a row's team field holds it.

query.name: created_after
query.description: Only reports started within this window (last_week, last_month and so on).

capabilities.intent: List the account's manual-testing reports - Workflow Analyzer, Assisted Tests or PDF Scanner - newest first, with each report's id, name, creator, status, issue counts and score, filterable by name, person, team and date - use this to find someone's latest manual reports or a report by name.
guidance: Link a row with its bare id, never uniqueId: Workflow Analyzer as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/workflow-analyzer/report?ids={id}, Assisted Test as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/assisted-test/report?ar_ids={id}. The same address works in every region.
product is required; without it the call answers 422 'Parameter product is required'.
Paging is page and page_size; info.count is the total, info.next the next page number or null. A page can hold fewer rows than page_size when a report is still being created.

isColdStart true means this page came back empty with no filter sent (product other than extension). On page 1 that means the account has no reports of that product, and the rows, if any, are BrowserStack sample reports. Past the last page it is also true, with reports [], info.count 0 and info.page 1, so read info.next rather than paging until empty. A filtered empty result and product=extension always answer false.

Workflow Analyzer and Assisted Test rows share a shape: id, uniqueId ('workflowScan:<id>' or 'assistiveTest:<id>'), testType, time, issues, issueSummary, score, wcagVersion {label,value}. PDF Scanner rows differ: issueCount instead of issues, timestamp instead of time, and th_build_id.
createdBy is an object of id and name; team is the team (sub-group) id.
Use user_id to narrow to one person rather than reading every page.

200.description: One page of manual-product reports, newest first; no success wrapper.

count.description: Total matching rows across all pages.

next.description: Next page number; null on the last page.

isColdStart.description: true = no own reports; any rows are BrowserStack samples.

uniqueId.description: workflowScan:<id> or assistiveTest:<id>; absent on PDF rows.

testType.description: workflowScan or assistiveTest; absent on PDF rows.

issueSummary.description: Counts per severity on WA/AT rows; on PDF rows an object of profile -> {issueCount,isFailed}.

pageCount.description: null on failed PDF Scanner reports.

capabilities.name: list_build_report_runs

query.name: project_id
query.description: TestHub project id (testRuns[].projectId, or a Website Scanner scan id) to list one project's builds. Wins over project_name when both are sent.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Exact project name, used only when project_id is absent.

query.name: build_name
query.description: Exact build name (testRuns[].name); every numbered run of that build comes back.

query.name: query
query.description: Free-text match on build name.

query.name: central_scanner
query.description: Send true, together with project_id = the scan id, to list a Website Scanner scan's runs. Leave it out for Automated Tests builds.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number; follow info.next.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Builds per page.

query.name: sort_by
query.description: TestHub sort key and direction.

query.name: source
query.description: Only lcnc is accepted (Low Code Automation parent builds); any other value answers 422.

capabilities.intent: List the account's Automated Tests builds (or one Website Scanner scan's runs) newest first, with build name, number, project, status, creator and issue summary - use this to find a build and the thBuildId every other build report capability needs.
guidance: Link an Automated Tests build as https://accessibility.browserstack.com/automated-tests/projects/{projectName}/builds/{name}/{buildNumber}?thBuildId={thBuildId}, every value from the same row and URL-encoded (a space is %20). A Website Scanner run is https://accessibility.browserstack.com/site-scanner/projects/{scan name}/builds?thBuildId={thBuildId}, with the scan's display name from list_website_scanner_scans, never the CS_<name>_CS projectName. The same address works in every region.
thBuildId is the key every build report capability takes as th_build_id. Pair it with name, buildNumber and projectName when talking to the user.
testRuns[].id is the TestHub build id, NOT the local id that meta and overview return as id. Never pass it anywhere.
Paging: follow info.next until it is null. info.count is not a total; it grows page by page.

summary is present only when the build has test cases and status is completed, processing, finalizing or timeout. A build whose status says completed but has no test cases is reported as status failed, with failureBucket when known.
Without project_id the list holds every Automated Tests build in the account; Website Scanner runs are left out. central_scanner=true without project_id returns an empty testRuns list.
For a Website Scanner scan, send central_scanner=true and project_id = the scan id; each run is a build named "Build".

200.description: Builds page: testRuns plus TestHub paging info (no data wrapper). From a live call.

count.description: not a total; grows page by page

prev.description: next/previous page number; null at the end

next.description: next/previous page number; null at the end

capabilities.name: search_build_report_runs

query.name: query
query.description: Text to match in build names.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Exact project name to search within. Empty means all projects.

query.name: project_id
query.description: TestHub project id; wins over project_name.

query.name: build_name
query.description: Exact build name.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number; follow info.next.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Builds per page.

capabilities.intent: Search the account's Automated Tests builds by name text, optionally inside one project - use this to find a build the user names and get its thBuildId.
guidance: Same code and response shape as list_build_report_runs. Only the dashboard's search box calls this path.
No match is 200 with testRuns [], not 404.
thBuildId is what the build report capabilities take as th_build_id. testRuns[].id is a TestHub id: do not use it.
Paging: follow info.next until null. info.count is not a total.

200.description: Same shape as the build list: testRuns plus info. From a live call.

count.description: not a total; grows page by page

prev.description: next/previous page number; null at the end

next.description: next/previous page number; null at the end

capabilities.name: get_build_report_metadata

path_params.name: project_name
path_params.description: Not read: the build is found by th_build_id alone. Send the project name or any placeholder.

path_params.name: test_run_name
path_params.description: Not read. The dashboard sends "name#number" for builds and the literal "Build" for Website Scanner runs; any value works.

query.name: th_build_id
query.description: The build's thBuildId from list_build_report_runs.

query.name: central_scanner
query.description: Send true for a Website Scanner run. Leave it OUT for an Automated Tests build: any value, even false, counts as true and answers 404.

capabilities.intent: Read a build's or scan run's report header - name, build number, creator, dates, status, WCAG version, engine version, settings, browser and OS, SDK and CI info, and severity counts.
guidance: The path segments are ignored; only th_build_id picks the build.
central_scanner must match the build's kind. A mismatch (or th_build_id missing) is 404 "TestRun Not Found", the same error as a wrong id.
metaData.id is the local report id, not the TestHub id that the build list returns as id.
metaData.wcagVersion is a display label ("WCAG 2.1 AA"), while the build list gives the raw value (wcag21aa).
metaData.hasFailedAdvancedScan and metaData.isFupDenied flag partial scans; metaData.loadLimitReachedFailure means the plan's load limit was hit.
Website Scanner runs carry sessionData only. Automated Tests builds also carry ciInfo, versionControl, hostInfo and sdk* fields.

200.description: Report header under metaData, plus info. From a live call (Automated Tests build).

capabilities.name: get_build_report_overview

query.name: th_build_id
query.description: The build's thBuildId.

query.name: central_scanner
query.description: true for a Website Scanner run; leave it OUT for an Automated Tests build (any value counts as true).

capabilities.intent: Read a build's or scan run's overview - issue counts by severity, pages and components, test health, issue and score trends over earlier builds, the comparison with the previous build, and issue counts by URL, category and component.
guidance: data.issueSummary holds the severity counts plus issueCount, pageCount, componentCount and aiIssuesCount.

capabilities.intent: Hide (or unhide) accessibility issues in one report at issue, component, rule or guideline scope, with a reason - the dashboard's Hide issue action. Changes the report's issue counts and score.

A request to make the change, however specific, is not that yes: ask first, and send user_permission granted only after it.

Confirm with the user before every call: it changes the report every viewer sees, and with persist true it carries into later builds. When hiding, ask for the reason by offering exactly these six, the only ones the API takes: Duplicate, Not relevant, Not a priority, False positive, Technical challenges, Others. 'Not an issue' is not a hide reason: it is a needs-review decision (review_needs_review_issue).

Read before you ask: get the exact findings this will change first (list_build_issues_by_guideline or list_build_issues_by_rule for a build or scan run, get_workflow_analyzer_consolidated_report for a Workflow Analyzer report), and put their count, rule or guideline and report in the preview. An approval asked for without the count is an approval of an unknown change.
Undo is the same call with hidden false and the same scope, rule_id/guideline_tag, component_id and issue_id; reason is then not needed.

502 'Could not record this change. Nothing was changed' means TestHub refused the write; nothing changed, so it is safe to retry once.
422 'Invalid parameters passed. Parameter reason is required.' means hidden was true without a reason.

200.description: From code (issues_controller#hide): a success renders only {success: true}.

capabilities.intent: Confirm a needs-review issue as a real issue, mark it Not an issue, or put it back to pending - the single-issue review on the dashboard.
guidance: APPROVAL FIRST: before calling, tell the user exactly what will change (what, where, how many) and wait for an explicit yes in their own words ('yes', 'go ahead', 'approved'). A request to make the change, however specific, is not that yes: ask first, and send user_permission granted only after it. Here 'confirm it as a real issue' names the decision the user wants; it is not approval to record it.

Confirm with the user before every call. To undo a decision made here, call this again with confirmed null and hidden false: the issue goes back to pending. This works whether or not the issue has a reviewCategory; undo_bulk_review_decisions only reverses decisions made through bulk review and answers 422 'not found for undo review' for the rest. Read before you ask: find the exact finding first and name it, its rule and its page in the preview. For a build or scan run: get_build_issue.

Only issues whose result is needs-review take this: any other issue answers 422 'Invalid issue type'. A combination outside the three states above answers 422 'Issue that needs review can't be updated to the requested state.'

An option's outcome, not its label, decides the result: on Images (and Links) opt-yes is outcome dismiss and opt-no is confirm. Read outcome before choosing.

workflow_analyzer_report.title: Workflow Analyzer report
workflow_analyzer_report.description: The accessibility issues the Workflow Analyzer browser extension found on the web pages or flow one person scanned.
workflow_analyzer_report.id_convention: A plain integer, discovered through the report list; it is the workflowReportId the accessibility issue tool reads.
key_facts: Reports are shared across the account, so the list holds everyone's; one person's are picked out by the creator on each row.
A report is created by scanning in the browser extension; there is nothing to create or delete here.

website_scan.title: Website scan
website_scan.description: A Website Scanner scan: a saved set of web page addresses and accessibility settings, run once or on a recurring basis.
website_scan.id_convention: A plain integer, discovered through the scan list or returned when a scan is started; a name is resolved to its id through that list.

relations.via: runs once, or again on each recurrence

key_facts: A scan's own row carries only its latest run; the earlier runs are listed per scan.
Scans are shared across the account, so the list holds everyone's.

scan_run.title: Scan run
scan_run.description: One run of a Website Scanner scan, with the accessibility issues its pages had at that time.
scan_run.id_convention: A plain integer, read together with its scan's id; discovered through the scan's run list.
key_facts: A page that did not load in a run is still counted as scanned in some places; the run's failure count says how many did not load.

automated_tests_project.title: Automated Tests project
automated_tests_project.description: A named group of web test builds that ran with accessibility checks on, usually one per test suite or site.
automated_tests_project.id_convention: A plain integer; builds are narrowed to a project by its name, not by this id.

relations.via: groups the builds reported under its name

key_facts: A project is created by the first test run reported under its name; there is nothing to create or delete here.

automated_tests_build.title: Automated Tests build
automated_tests_build.description: One run of web tests with accessibility checks on, through Automate or the BrowserStack SDK, and the issues its pages produced.
automated_tests_build.id_convention: A 40-character string of lowercase letters and digits, the thBuildId in the build's dashboard link; discovered through the build list.
key_facts: A build appears only if its tests ran with accessibility checks on.
status is the accessibility report's; a completed report whose build ran no tests reads failed.

assisted_test_report.title: Assisted Test report
assisted_test_report.description: The issues one guided Assisted Test recorded on a web page: keyboard, forms, modals, images, tables and similar checks.
assisted_test_report.id_convention: A plain integer, discovered through the report list.
key_facts: Its individual issues are read on the Accessibility dashboard; the list gives its counts.

bulk_review_category.title: Bulk review category
bulk_review_category.description: A group of similar issues reviewed together in one pass (bulk review).
bulk_review_category.id_convention: Ids come from the category list.

comparison.title: Report comparison
comparison.description: Two runs of the same report compared: new, fixed and unchanged issues.
comparison.id_convention: Takes the two runs' ids; each capability names them.

custom_dashboard.title: Custom dashboard
custom_dashboard.description: A saved cross-report view of accessibility trends, scores and issues over chosen projects, scans and reports.
custom_dashboard.id_convention: A plain integer id, from the custom dashboard list.

guideline.title: WCAG guideline
guideline.description: A WCAG success criterion, such as 1.1.1 Non-text Content, that issues are grouped by.

integration.title: Ticket link
integration.description: A link between accessibility issues and an existing issue-tracker ticket (e.g. Jira).
integration.id_convention: Ticket keys as the tracker shows them.

issue.title: Issue
issue.description: One accessibility violation found on a page element, which can be hidden or marked for review.
issue.id_convention: Ids come from the report's issue routes.

report.title: Report
report.description: One accessibility report of any product (Workflow Analyzer, Assisted Test, Automated Tests build, Website Scanner run).
report.id_convention: Id format depends on the product; each capability names which one it takes.

test_case.title: Test case
test_case.description: One test or page inside a report run, with its own issues.
test_case.id_convention: Ids come from the report's test case list.

test_run.title: Report run
test_run.description: One report's run on the dashboard: an Automated Tests build or a Website Scanner run, with its issues and pages.
test_run.id_convention: Dashboard routes address it by name or build uuid; each capability says which.

user.title: User
user.description: The signed-in BrowserStack user, with their group, role and plan.
user.id_convention: Not needed; the call answers for the caller.

website_scan_activity.title: Website Scanner scan activity
website_scan_activity.description: A Website Scanner scan seen from the dashboard: its overview, issue trend across runs, per-page logs, and re-running it.

false_positive_feedback.title: False-positive feedback
false_positive_feedback.description: One issue pattern a user confirmed is not a real problem, saved per rule to filter it from later reports.
false_positive_feedback.id_convention: A string starting with fp_, returned when the feedback is saved and on each entry of the memory.
key_facts: The memory belongs to the account: every user's agent reads it. An entry applies to the site it was saved on, or to all sites when global.
fetchAccessibilityIssues already brings the memory for the rules of the issues it answers with.

Unauthorized.description: The username or access key was not accepted ('Invalid credentials.'), or the plan has no API access ('You do not have access to External APIs.').

Forbidden.description: The caller's role cannot view builds and reports, or the account is restricted to another region.

InvalidPageToken.description: next_page was not a token from this list or had expired. On the Website Scanner lists, a limit that differs from the previous page also answers 422.

PagingChanged.description: limit or project_name differs from the request that produced next_page.

ScanNotFound.description: No scan with this id in the account: error is 'Scan builds not found'.

UpstreamFailure.description: The service holding the list did not answer; retry shortly.

InternalServerError.description: The list could not be read; retry shortly.

DashboardUnauthorized.description: The token was not accepted, or the user could not be found. Credentials are re-minted on the next call; persistent 401 means the account itself was refused.

DashboardForbidden.description: The user's own role, plan, feature flag, ownership rule or region refuses this, exactly as it would in the dashboard.

DashboardScopeNotAllowed.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_SCOPE: this route is not on the ai_agent allowlist. Not fixable by retrying; it needs a backend allowlist change.

DashboardNotFound.description: No such record for this account.

DashboardBadRequest.description: A parameter was missing or malformed.

DashboardUnprocessable.description: The parameters were understood but not usable (e.g. a required one is missing).

DashboardUpstreamFailure.description: A service behind the dashboard did not answer; retry shortly.

FpMemoryDisabled.description: The caller's role cannot act on issues, or false-positive memory is not enabled for this account (error says which).

FpFeedbackRejected.description: The feedback was not saved: unknown rule, a root cause or predicate too thin to match later issues by, a pageUrl without a host, or the rule already holds 1000 entries. error says which.

FpFeedbackDuplicate.description: Not saved: an active entry already covers the same rule, site (or all sites), scope and predicate. data.existingId names it.
